text:
incident-bot: PAGER: high CPU OOMs observed on tokenizer pods in prod-us-west1. 75% of tokenizer-* pods have restarted in last 10m. Suspected prompt-processing spike. Alerting oncall. https://prometheus/redwood/alerts/2391112222 :rotating_light:

maria: ack — jumping in. seeing a bunch of `OOMKilled` on tokenizer-preproc-*. pods. no GPU errors in logs, just CPU saturation and kernel OOM messages.

aj: oncall here. thanks for the ping. can someone paste a representative pod log? also what's the customer impact?

dave: quick snippet from `kubectl describe` on one of the pods:

```
Name: tokenizer-preproc-78b9f
Status: Running
Last State: Terminated
Reason: OOMKilled
Message: container killed due to out-of-memory
Exit Code: 137
```

No stack traces beyond repeated `tokenize_worker` allocations.

ellen: repros line up with a large prompt churn we started seeing at 13:04UTC — big customers started sending > 20k-token prompts with dense regexes. prefix caching isn't hitting.

maria: customer-impact: support queue shows ~120 failed requests in last 15m, concentrated on a single enterprise tenant using bulk ingest. retries are spiking but most backoffs eventually succeed after a minute. marking as potential P2->P1 if error rate grows.

aj: immediate mitigation options: (1) throttle inbound prompt size via rate-limiter rule for that tenant, (2) scale tokenizer replicas vertically (cpu) or temporally, (3) reduce batch size / disable some preproc operators. which is fastest?

ellen: quickest is to add a temporary rate-limit rule in the API gateway for that tenant — we can do that in <2m. second fastest is to patch the configmap to reduce `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS` from 2048 to 512 and rollout.

maria: i'll open a gateway throttle now. aj, can you prepare the configmap patch?

aj: applying gateway throttle: `curl -X POST https://gw.internal/rate-limits -d '{"tenant_id":"ten-1234","limit_rps":10}'` — response 200. telling support-bot to update customer status. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Automated update posted to customer status page for ten-1234: "We are throttling request rate due to processing instability; retries should resume within minutes."

aj: patching configmap to reduce batch size and restart tokenizer DaemonSet (rolling).

```
kubectl patch configmap tokenizer-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"MAX_BATCH_TOKENS":"512"}}'
kubectl rollout restart ds/tokenizer-preproc -n prod
```

aj: patch applied and rollouts started. monitoring pods.

dave: observed a node with repeated pod evictions — suspect node-level pressure. Running cordon/drain on node `gke-uswest1-pool-4-xyz` for stability.

```
kubectl cordon gke-uswest1-pool-4-xyz
kubectl drain gke-uswest1-pool-4-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

aj: cordon/drain done. pods are rescheduling onto other nodes. watch for increased scheduling failures.

maria: telemetry after throttle + configmap change: CPU 75th-99th percentile for tokenizer pods dropped ~40% in 5m. restart rate down from 75% to 8% of pods in the group. error rate for that tenant down to baseline.

ellen: nice. can we also apply a quick evict-threshold tweak to kubelet to avoid cascading OOM-driven restarts? or is that too risky prod-wide?

aj: prefer targeted mitigations first. i'll open a short-lived autoscaler increase for tokenizer node pool to give breathing room for background reschedules.

```
gcloud container clusters update prod-us-west1 --node-pool tokenizer-pool --num-nodes 8
```

ops-bot: Autoscaler increase requested; new nodes provisioning (expected ~3-4m).

maria: customer impact update: support notified enterprise contact. no broader customer degradation observed. marking incident as mitigated for active degradation but keeping P1 until stabilised for 1h.

dave: a couple of pods still show kernel logs with `kswapd` churn and `memory cgroup` throttling. recommend we capture heap/core dump and open a ticket for the tokenizer preprocess memory leak investigation.

aj: triggering memory dump on a failing pod:

```
kubectl exec -n prod tokenizer-preproc-78b9f -- bash -c "curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:1234/debug/dump > /tmp/memdump.tar"
kubectl cp prod/tokenizer-preproc-78b9f:/tmp/memdump.tar ./memdump-2391112222.tar
```

aj: memdump grabbed and uploaded to artifact store: gs://redwood-incident-artifacts/2391112222/memdump.tar

ellen: adding post-incident actions: (1) add prompt size-based circuit breaker per tenant, (2) CAP batch token default lower, (3) perf test for regex-heavy prompts. I'll PR runbook updates.

sre-rotation: i'm taking over the incident for the midnight handoff. summary: root cause suspected tokenizer preproc blowup due to large regex-heavy prompts from ten-1234 causing sustained CPU OOMs and node pressure. mitigations done: gateway throttle applied, batch size reduced, offending node cordoned, node pool temporarily increased, memdumps captured. current state: error rate normalised, restart rate low. followups: deeper memory investigation, runbook updates, tenant rate-limits.

maria: thanks — i'll write the incident timeline and assign follow-ups to research and dev teams. handing off paging to night oncall. :handshake:

aj: leaving notes in incident channel and creating jira RED-INC-2391 for the post-mortem and long-term fixes. good job team. :tada:
